paper_title: Fused Benzothiadiazole: A Building Block for n-Type Organic Acceptor to Achieve High-Performance Organic Solar Cells
source_file: /home/wzfeng/MySearch/PhotoRag/MD/Advanced Materials - 2019 - Yuan - Fused Benzothiadiazole  A Building Block for n‐Type Organic Acceptor to Achieve/auto/Advanced Materials - 2019 - Yuan - Fused Benzothiadiazole  A Building Block for n‐Type Organic Acceptor to Achieve.md

knowledge_points.content: The Y5 acceptor is designed with an A-DAD-A molecular structure featuring a ladder-type electron-deficient-core (TPBT) and 1,1-dicyanomethylene-3-indanone (INCN) end-cap groups.
knowledge_points.evidence: A new n-OS acceptor, Y5, with an electron-deficient-core-based fused structure is designed and synthesized... by introducing a ladder-type electron-deficient-core-based central fused ring (TPBT) and INCN as end-cap group.

knowledge_points.content: The introduction of the electron-deficient benzothiadiazole (BT) unit into the central core of Y5 creates a planar DAD fused structure that enhances the delocalization of pi-electrons and facilitates electron migration.
knowledge_points.evidence: By using DAD fused core one could also adopt a relatively planar structure rather than a twisted one and hence facilitate the electron migration from the donor to acceptor since the planarized DAD enhances the delocalization of pi electrons.

knowledge_points.content: Y5-based organic solar cells achieve high power conversion efficiencies (PCE) across different donors: 11.0% with J61, 13.1% with TTFQx-T1, and a peak of 14.1% with PBDB-T.
knowledge_points.evidence: As a result, the power conversion efficiency of the Y5-based OSCs with J61, TTFQx-T1, and PBDB-T reaches 11.0%, 13.1%, and 14.1%, respectively.

knowledge_points.content: Y5 exhibits a narrow optical bandgap of 1.38 eV, with an absorption onset at 900 nm and a high extinction coefficient of 1.24 x 10^5 cm^-1.
knowledge_points.evidence: The absorption onset of the Y5 film is located at 900 nm (Eg = 1.38 eV) with an absorption coefficient of 1.24 x 10^5 cm^-1.

knowledge_points.content: The HOMO and LUMO energy levels of the Y5 acceptor are -5.55 eV and -3.87 eV, respectively, determined via cyclic voltammetry.
knowledge_points.evidence: the highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) and lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) energy levels were calculated to be -5.55 and -3.87 eV, respectively.

knowledge_points.content: GIWAXS analysis of Y5 neat films reveals a preferred face-on orientation with a pi-pi stacking distance of approximately 3.63 Angstroms (q = 1.73 Angstroms^-1) in the out-of-plane direction.
knowledge_points.evidence: Y5 shows a preferred face-on orientation with a strong pi-pi stacking peak in the out-of-plane (OOP) direction at q = 1.73 A^-1 (d ≈ 3.63 A).

knowledge_points.content: The Y5 acceptor shows a high electron mobility of 2.71 x 10^-4 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1, measured by the space-charge-limited current (SCLC) method.
knowledge_points.evidence: the electron mobility (µe) of Y5 is... an average value of 1.71 x 10^-4 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1 (measured by the space-charge-limited current (SCLC) method). Note: Abstract cites 2.71 x 10^-4.

knowledge_points.content: High energetic disorder (sigma) in the bulk heterojunction blend, such as the 105 meV found in J61:Y5, correlates with a significantly decreased fill factor (FF) due to hole trapping.
knowledge_points.evidence: a larger sigma (105 meV) of the J61:Y5 BHJ blend could lead to the significantly decreased FF of 59%... holes can be more easily trapped at these tailed states and combine with electrons.

knowledge_points.content: Optimized PBDB-T:Y5 devices exhibit an internal quantum efficiency (IQE) plateau reaching 80% between 550 and 820 nm, indicating efficient charge carrier collection.
knowledge_points.evidence: The maximum IQE plateau reaches 80% from 550 to 820 nm, suggesting the effective charge carriers collection at the electrodes.

knowledge_points.content: Optimization of the PBDB-T:Y5 device morphology involves the use of 0.5 vol% chloronaphthalene (CN) solvent additive and thermal annealing at 110 °C for 10 minutes.
knowledge_points.evidence: The PBDB-T:Y5 device at optimum condition... Under 0.5% CN with thermal annealing at 110 °C for 10 min.

knowledge_points.content: Device optimization for PBDB-T:Y5 leads to more balanced charge transport, with the electron/hole mobility ratio improving from 1.85 (as-cast) to 1.25 (optimized).
knowledge_points.evidence: the µe/µh values of the PBDB-T:Y5 blend are evaluated to be... (with a µe/µh ratio of 1.85) for the as-cast film and... (with a µe/µh ratio of 1.25) for the optimized film.

knowledge_points.content: Y5 demonstrates good thermal stability with a 5% weight loss onset temperature of 340 °C and exhibits a crystalline nature with a melting temperature (Tm) of 331 °C.
knowledge_points.evidence: the onset temperature with 5% weight loss of Y5 was 340 °C... DSC plot of Y5... shows clear melting temperature (Tm) at 331 °C.

knowledge_points.content: The power-law component (alpha) for the light intensity dependence of Jsc in optimized PBDB-T:Y5 devices is 0.97, indicating that bimolecular recombination is effectively suppressed.
knowledge_points.evidence: The alpha value of optimized film (0.97) was closer to unity than that of the as-cast film (0.95)... the results showed that bimolecular recombination was suppressed more effectively in the optimized films.
